question: Follicles are seen on the palpebral conjunctiva in bacterial conjunctivitis, while papillae are the hallmark of viral conjunctivitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. The association is reversed: follicles = viral/chlamydial; papillae = bacterial/allergic. A giant papillary reaction (cobblestone appearance) is characteristic of vernal keratoconjunctivitis and contact-lens allergy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Follicles (lymphoid aggregates with central avascular cores) are the hallmark of VIRAL (and chlamydial) conjunctivitis. Papillae (vascular cores surrounded by inflammatory cells) are seen in bacterial and allergic conjunctivitis.
